newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens gives no comment on power merger.
newsitem.headline: Siemens gives no comment on power merger.

text.p: German industrial conglomerate Siemens AG on Tuesday said its power generation unit expected "ordinary" results this year as a result of price competition for big contracts.

Unit chief Adolf Huettl, speaking at a news conference called to review 1995/96 results, also declined to comment on reports Siemens planned to merge its fossil-fuel power operations with those of U.S. Westinghouse Electric Co..
"Siemens as a rule does not comment on rumours," Huettl told reporters.
Huettl said price competition led to the 3.6 percent drop in sales reported for 1995-96, which ended September 30. Pretax profit in 1995-96 was 410 million marks ($258.1 million), up from 79 million.

Last week the deputy chairman of Siemens' supervisory board and head of the firm's works council, Alfons Graf, confirmed the group was in talks with Westinghouse about a joint venture in power operations.
The two firms were interested in founding the venture this year with its headquarters in the United States, Siemens sources said.

At the news conference, Huettl said fossil-fuel generation remains a core business of KWU. He also said Siemens has no plans to split off its atomic power operations, but did not rule out cooperating with other companies.
